subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 4-year-old boy is evaluated for behavioral problems and difficulty hearing. His mother reports that he is defiant and physically aggressive at preschool. Examination shows mild coarse facial features and short stature, with firm hepatomegaly. Slit-lamp examination shows completely clear corneas. A maternal uncle had similar facial features and aggressive behavior and died of heart failure at age 25.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible?
explanation_correct: Hunter syndrome (mucopolysaccharidosis type II) is the only mucopolysaccharidosis inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern, and it results from deficiency of iduronate-2-sulfatase. Affected boys show a milder Hurler-like picture with coarse features, hepatosplenomegaly, and developmental problems, but corneal clouding is characteristically absent. Aggressive behavior and hearing loss are common, and the maternal uncle in this family is consistent with X-linked transmission.

explanation_incorrect.B: α-L-Iduronidase deficiency causes Hurler syndrome, which is autosomal recessive and features prominent corneal clouding.
explanation_incorrect.C: N-Acetylglucosaminyl-1-phosphotransferase deficiency causes I-cell disease, which is more severe than Hurler syndrome and is associated with markedly elevated plasma lysosomal enzymes.
explanation_incorrect.D: α-Galactosidase A deficiency causes Fabry disease, with angiokeratomas, acroparesthesias, and renal disease rather than skeletal and facial changes.
explanation_incorrect.E: Galactocerebrosidase deficiency causes Krabbe disease, an infantile demyelinating leukodystrophy.

educationalObjective: Hunter syndrome is an X-linked deficiency of iduronate-2-sulfatase that mimics Hurler syndrome but spares the cornea and is often accompanied by aggressive behavior.
